UT-2026-SB234.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking, Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Air Quality
UT-2026-SB234.aiSummary: The bill changes Utah rules for environmental health and waste management, including air quality. It says state agencies could not start new rule changes for certain pollution limits if they are stricter or broader than federal rules, and if there is no federal standard, the agency would have to base the rule on the best available science and the weight of scientific evidence. It also says some rules are exempt and sets an effective date of May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-SB21.aiSummary: This law updates Utah rules for geothermal resources, which are heat and related energy from the earth. It changes who owns geothermal resources on some lands, sets new definitions, and lets the state water rights division ask for more well information, keep some records private for a time, and require surety bonds, or payment guarantees, for wells. It affects landowners, operators, and people working with geothermal resources, including school and institutional trust lands.

UT-2026-HB416.aiSummary: This bill would change health coverage and support programs for first responders and volunteer emergency medical workers. It would create a firefighter cancer benefit fund, change how certain insurance tax money is used for firefighter retirement, and update who can get help through the volunteer emergency medical service insurance program. It would also require reports on mental health resources for first responders and create a fund to help pay for those resources for some small agencies.

UT-2026-HB269.aiSummary: This law changes how ambulance services are paid in Utah, including Medicaid, health plans, and workers' compensation claims. It also starts on July 1, 2026, and was signed into law.

UT-2026-HB110.policyArea: Board of Pardons and Parole, Bureau of Criminal Identification, Courts
UT-2026-HB110.aiSummary: It became law in Utah. It changes how courts, the Board of Pardons and Parole, and the Bureau of Criminal Identification handle some offenders, including when a court can order probation-style supervision for some class B misdemeanor cases. It also changes when the board may reconsider parole or a pardon for some people who reoffend, limits expungement eligibility for some registry offenders, and adds more steps before early release from prison.

UT-2026-HB401.aiSummary: The bill became law and directs Utah State University to study the geological and environmental effects of geothermal energy development in Utah. The study must look at underground conditions, different development methods, and effects at or near coal plant sites, and it must include ways to reduce harm. The university must report its findings to a legislative committee by the November interim meeting in 2027. It takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB296.policyArea: Environment, Great Salt Lake, Natural Resources
UT-2026-HB296.aiSummary: The bill would let water providers include a commitment of available water for uses on the Great Salt Lake in their water conservation plans. It also would make other changes to the rules for those plans, including public notice, filing, and updates every five years. Water providers would need to follow these rules to receive state funds for water development. The bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB125.policyArea: Boating, Department of Natural Resources, Environment
UT-2026-HB125.aiSummary: The bill makes several changes to Utah laws on natural resources, boating, water rights, and wildlife. It changes invasive mussel rules for boats and other gear, updates fees and records for boat liveries and water rights, and changes some duties in state agencies. It also creates a cultural site stewardship program and repeals some older sections of law.
